about: Released 0.2.0 runtime platform status, from recorded package evidence only. A cross-build or a newer source test is not release qualification. scripts/catalogue.py reads this file, checks every evidence path exists, and publishes it in the layer catalogue. The current facade source may have newer platform paths than this released-package status.

statuses.supported: The runtime installs, starts its background services, becomes ready, recovers from a crash and uninstalls, and an application's default resolution reaches it.
statuses.supported without background services: The programs install, run in the foreground and uninstall. No background service is registered, and default resolution finds no runtime.
statuses.unsupported: The released package has no qualified protected runtime service on this platform. Its default resolution and protected calls remain unavailable.

platforms.name: Windows x64, per-user installation
platforms.runtime: Per-user MSI; the supervisor starts the runtime in the signed-in session.
limits: Windows x64 installation and upgrade are qualified for 0.2.0. Windows MSI packages are unsigned.
ARM64 is cross-built; installation on ARM64 hardware is untested.

evidence.shows: 0.2.0 candidate: fresh per-user installation, cross-tool calls, upgrade from 0.1.7, reinstall, custom-folder upgrade, forced-failure rollback and complete removal passed.

platforms.name: Windows x64, machine installation
platforms.runtime: Machine MSI; a service template starts a per-session runtime for each signed-in user.
limits: Everyone installation requires elevation. Runtime instances run in each signed-in user session.
ARM64 is cross-built; installation on ARM64 hardware is untested.

evidence.shows: 0.2.0 candidate: machine installation, upgrade and forced-failure rollback, fresh-session startup, crash recovery and removal passed.

platforms.name: Linux amd64 with a systemd user manager
platforms.runtime: Per-user tarball; install.sh registers abstraction-runtime.service with the user manager.
limits: Trusted selection needs clone3 and waitid P_PIDFD (Linux 5.4 or newer); a sandbox denying them returns PROOF_UNAVAILABLE.
Lifecycle evidence covers WSL2 and a hosted Ubuntu amd64 runner. ARM64 installation, other distributions and graphical sessions are untested.

evidence.shows: 0.2.0 candidate on hosted Ubuntu: installation under a disposable account and systemd user manager, readiness, a real download, result observation, removal with retained data and process cleanup passed.

platforms.name: Linux amd64 without a systemd user manager (containers, WSL without systemd, hosted CI accounts)
platforms.runtime: The same tarball; install.sh installs the programs, reports that no background service will run and records `timer no`.
limits: Default resolution cannot select a runtime: selection reads the loaded user unit from systemctl, so applications receive runtime_unavailable.
`openabstractions serve runtime` runs in the foreground; an application reaches it only through an explicit endpoint.

evidence.shows: 0.2.0 release: installation without a user manager, the openabstractions payload, absence of retired jobd/dl/jobctl executables and removal passed. This job does not establish foreground capability calls.

platforms.name: macOS (universal package)
platforms.runtime: The released 0.2.0 runtime installs and runs; its protected calls and default resolution remain unqualified.
limits: The released 0.2.0 package lacks the Program proof needed by protected calls.
Current development source uses macOS XPC for Program proof and installed-runtime selection. Native tests cover that source path; package installation and end-to-end qualification remain open.

evidence.shows: 0.2.0 universal package built, signed, notarised and stapled. Package availability does not establish protected-call readiness; the documented identity limitation remains.
Install, upgrade and crash recovery pass; readiness, resolution and held work are REFUSED-BY-PLATFORM-LIMIT.
Native launchd start, recovery and removal; typed status fails on process proof.
Current source has a macOS XPC installed-runtime selector. This source path does not change the released 0.2.0 package status.

platforms.name: Android, including Termux
platforms.runtime: None. No runtime is built, packaged, installed or run for Android.
limits: The packager builds only linux and macos; the release builds Windows MSIs, Linux tarballs and one macOS package.
Termux has no systemd user manager, which Linux selection requires.

evidence.shows: The release builds no Android asset.
Nothing in the tree records a build, install or run on Android or Termux.
